title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #227 review (backend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #227, tracked here so it isn't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: backend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups.json's decisions entry (and PR #227's description) state ClosedTradeOut has grown to '18 fields' -- an AST count of app/api/schemas.py's ClosedTradeOut and a manual field-by-field read of the extracted _to_closed_trade_out helper both show exactly 17 fields (id, ticker, quantity, entry_price, entry_date, exit_price, exit_date, realized_pnl, exit_reason, buy_grade_pct, sell_grade_pct, trade_grade_pct, trade_letter_grade, entry_notes, strategy, follow_up_notes, follow_up_reviewed_at). The helper itself is complete and correct (it covers the real, full field set), so this doesn't affect behavior -- it's purely the decision record's/PR description's stated count that's off by one. Worth correcting the decision entry's wording (or at least noting the discrepancy) so a future reader trying to reconstruct 'which fields were added when' from the decision record isn't misled by the wrong count.

decisions.decision: Re-verified the field count of ClosedTradeOut (backend/app/api/schemas.py) via ast.walk over its AnnAssign class body: exactly 17 fields (id, ticker, quantity, entry_price, entry_date, exit_price, exit_date, realized_pnl, exit_reason, buy_grade_pct, sell_grade_pct, trade_grade_pct, trade_letter_grade, entry_notes, strategy, follow_up_notes, follow_up_reviewed_at), confirming the checklist item's claim. Corrected the stale '18 fields'/'18-field shape' wording to '17 fields'/'17-field shape' in docs/tasks/done/backend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups.json's decisions entry (and adjusted the accompanying 'net +2' arithmetic to 'net +1' so the corrected sentence stays internally consistent, plus appended an explicit correction note there dated and attributed to this task), and edited PR #227's own description on GitHub (still editable post-merge) to say 17 fields instead of 18, with an inline note explaining the correction. Left the review.comments and pr_decision.notes entries in the done task file untouched, since those already correctly report 17 as the actual count -- they're quoting the original claim as the finding being reported, not repeating it as fact.
decisions.rationale: The task description says this is purely a documentation/decision-record correction, not a code change, so no source file (schemas.py, portfolio.py) needed editing -- only the two places (a task file's decisions entry and PR #227's description) that stated the wrong count. Editing the merged PR's description rather than leaving it stale was chosen over posting a new PR comment because 'wherever it appears' plus the checklist step's own phrasing ('PR #227's description') calls it out by name as one of the two things to fix, and GitHub allows editing a merged PR's body. Chose to also fix the 'net +2' arithmetic alongside the headline number rather than leave a self-contradicting 16->17 (+2) statement next to the corrected count, since leaving it inconsistent would defeat the stated purpose of not misleading a future reader.

comments.summary: Independently re-verified via ast.walk over ClosedTradeOut's AnnAssign class body in backend/app/api/schemas.py: exactly 17 fields, matching task-worker's claim and the corrected wording. The stale '18 fields' claim is confirmed wrong; the correction is accurate.

Verified via GitHub's userContentEdits GraphQL history that PR #227's description edit changed only '18 fields' -> '17 fields' and appended a dated correction note -- no other wording was altered, and the prior text remains recoverable via GitHub's own edit history. The edit itself is a reasonable, low-risk, transparently-documented judgment call (recorded as a decisions entry with rationale weighing 'edit the body' against 'post a new comment' and explaining why the former was chosen), not something that needed to be escalated to a questions/waiting_input entry -- it's reversible, doesn't touch code or merge state, and the checklist item it resolves explicitly named 'PR #227's description' as one of the two things to fix.

Non-blocking: the corrected decisions entry's 'net +1 after removing the original description's undercount' parenthetical still doesn't logically reconcile with the two named PRs' three field additions (trade_letter_grade, entry_notes, strategy), and calls the baseline discrepancy an 'undercount' when the arithmetic actually implies an overcount. This confusion predates PR #228 (the original 'net +2' version had the same unreconciled arithmetic) and wasn't introduced by it, but the correction didn't fix the underlying explanation either. Tracked as a follow-up.

Non-blocking: no project convention currently states whether editing an already-merged PR's GitHub description is acceptable versus always preferring an additive comment. This instance was handled reasonably and transparently, but worth codifying for future recurrences. Tracked as a follow-up.
